chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Fletcher's cool reply about his girlfriend Muriel Zalinger
summary: When a bandsman needled Fletcher that a dancer was holding his girl in Chicago, he calmly said he never had her to begin with, ending the jokes. Horace says he inherited his father's inward coolness.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: One time one of the guys on the band -- they would get at Fletcher too, you know. He wasn't excused because he was the leader. You know, they played tricks on him too. And here's one I'm going to tell you now. Hawk and them were

talking, said, hey -- Fletcher was going with a girl in Chicago whose name was Muriel Zalinger. She was quite a beautiful girl, you know. And one time the band was playing, and Muriel was dancing with a guy. You know, he was dancing the ballads, you know how they get, real tight, you know; one of those smart alecks in the band said, "Hey, Smack, look at that guy, how he's holding your girl. He's about to take your girl."

So Fletcher, just like he always is, cool and calm, he said, "Well, I tell you. If he can take her, I never had her in the beginning." And I thought that was a great thing. Man, you could hear a pin drop in there. It wasn't a joke anymore, see. Well, he said it, and I've never forgotten that. So that's what you were saying -- so they didn't play any more jokes on Smack after that.
He aced them out of that one.

Yeah. He was cool -- then. Nothing bothered him. If it did, you didn't know it. If was inward. I think he took that after my father. My father was real cool about everything. See, and he kept everything inwardly, (Inaudible), which is bad, actually, because a lot of times if you are bothered about something and you can talk to somebody about it and let it out, you'll feel better.
